release_notes:
PRECONSOLIDATION PRESSURE (Pc) COMPUTED PROPERLY

The Casagrande construction on the CONSOL_GR sheet located its point of maximum curvature on the load step after the bend, which on a sharp knee is already the virgin line. Pc therefore snapped to a load-step midpoint (5.66 or 1.41 kg/cm2) a whole step away from where the curve actually bends. The point and its tangent are now taken on a smooth curve fitted through the readings; the construction is otherwise the same.

- Projects saved earlier carry the old Pc. It is recomputed from the stored readings when the project is opened, so the next report shows the new value. Nothing else in the record changes.
- A Pc you enter by hand (the override box) now moves the drawn construction to the point on the curve that gives your value, so the tangent and bisector on the graph stay genuine.
- The consolidation dialog's computed Pc now comes from the same code as the report; it had its own, older copy.

CBR: CORRECTED PENETRATION RESISTANCE IS NOW CORRECTED

The SW_T sheet's rows labelled CORRECTED PENETRATION RESISTANCE read the raw stress at 2.54 and 5.08 mm. They now hold the stress measured from the corrected origin (ASTM D1883), using the same seating offset the dashed tangent on the penetration graph draws. On curves with a seating toe this raises CBR by a few percent (about 2-10% at 2.54 mm, 1-3% at 5.08 mm); a curve without a toe is unchanged. Regenerating an issued report may therefore change its CBR values slightly.

Project files need no action. Use Template_Government_260629_170SS.xlsx for borehole projects and Template_Government_260817_TP.xlsx for projects containing test pits.
